doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Jazz Showcase name and the sixties Chicago clubs
summary: He explains the name, lists clubs where he ran off-night sessions, and says musicians were paid whatever was left.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, there’s a couple of detours but I’ll get to those.

Ok. So once again... So the Jazz Showcase was really more of - in the beginning days - was more of a presenting organization than looking at actually finding a location that would be a permanent home.

I derived the name from my initials of course, JS and jam sessions, and Jazz Showcase. So as I said we did the Gate of Horn, then we started doing stuff up on Rush Street, different places. And then on Wells Street when the hippie era was going in the sixties. We had a place at Mother Blues, at the Old Town Gate, at the Club Nickel, and I used to do off-night sessions there also. A place called The Window, I had people like Freddy Hubbard and Jackie McLean. We collected money and we paid them whatever. If there was something left, fine. Most of the time there wasn’t too much left.
So how did you support yourself then?
Well I was, I told you, I was doing other jobs.
Oh, at the same time! Oh ok.
